- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.4) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5–10 days.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.2) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 3–7% to account for risk aversion or market panic.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >10%), model overcorrects in next 3–7 days; apply downward bias of 5–10% for 5–10 days post-spike.
- If sentiment is rising (increasing over last 5 days), model tends to lag; forecast should be adjusted upward by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is falling (decreasing over last 5 days), model tends to overreact; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5–10 days.
- Mean reversion is strong in 3–5 day horizons; if forecast is >15% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 5–10% for next 3–5 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often misses long-term trend; if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive, align forecast with 14-day moving average of history.
